work_completed:
- **Cases and map.** 74 cases in 5 modules plus a README. Every KPI line (success-1, success-2, failure-1, failure-2) has cases, with the red reasons stated in the README.
- **Planted repository (I3).** A product is generated once per session (copier, then `rulesync generate`, reusing W2-110's generator). Each case copies it into a folder named `harbour/`, plants three tickets and commits clean. It then runs `gov adopt --lite --stage A0` as a child process, with no edit afterwards.
- **success-1, failure-1 (I1).**
  - After A0, the roster's `coordination_ticket` is the id of exactly one new ticket file.
  - That ticket has `class: coordination` and the title `harbour coordination`.
  - A0's record text names the ticket id and the roster path.
  - Both files are in A0's single commit and the tree is clean.
  - Through the hook, the orchestrator on the new ticket gets `ask` for two installs.
- **failure-2 (I3).** An engineer, test designer, auditor, a second orchestrator (by id and by WBS id) and an orchestrator with no ticket are each refused. The three workers are also refused when put on the new coordination ticket.
- **I2 defaults.**
  - (i) A roster naming an existing ticket by id or by WBS id: A0 keeps it, creates nothing, and the CTO decisions still follow the kept key.
  - (ii) A roster without the key: the parsed roster less the key is unchanged. A separate case also checks that comments and line order are preserved.
  - (iii) `tk` removed: A0 refuses with no traceback and writes nothing.
- **success-2.** The refusal is checked in five planted products: no key, no roster file, the product as generated, and a key naming no ticket by id and by WBS id. In each, the orchestrator and an engineer are both tested. The refusal must stay `deny`, name `GOV_TICKET`, name the roster file and the key, and not claim a key was set. The "claims a key was set" predicate is defined in README § "Success 2: the words".

discoveries:
- **A W2-110 unit test pins the old wording.** `tests/unit/guard/test_w2_110_cto_install.py:172` asserts `"Set the top-level key" in reason` for every fail-closed case. If the new words drop that sentence, this test goes red.
  - It is not in W2-113's `allowed_paths` (`tests/unit/adopt/test_w2_113*` only).
  - It is a decided-behaviour revision, so DEC-1156 (7) routes it to the CTO.
  - Either the engineer keeps "Set the top-level key" in the new text, or the CTO widens the ticket by that file.
- **W2-110's acceptance suite pins no wording.** Its assertions are `says_how_to_set_the_key` (names the file and the key), `tells_to_escalate`, and the decision (`test_w2_110_fail_closed.py:27`, `test_w2_110_others_refused.py:25`). It has no conflict with success-2, as long as the new text keeps both names.
- **The base text trips two checks.** It has "(set at adoption)" after its instruction (`src/gov/guard/install.py:339`) and never names `GOV_TICKET`.
- **Reading: "`<project>`" is the repository's folder name.** The template asks for no name (copier has no question, and no file in `template/governance/project/` holds one). The title check is exact: `harbour coordination`. An implementer who reads the name from elsewhere would fail it for a reason that is not a defect. README reading 1 flags it.
- **The vendored `tk create` writes the title as a `# <title>` heading**, not a frontmatter key. The suite reads the frontmatter `title` if present, else the first heading.
- **Relied on but not in `sources:` (so not in `Implements:`):** DEC-1156, DEC-1052, DEC-1155, DEC-820, DEC-963. DEC-1155's path case was not written, because no KPI line asks for it.
risks:
- **Stricter reading.** `test_a_roster_without_the_key_keeps_its_text_and_its_comments` rejects an A0 that re-serialises the roster (a YAML dump). I2 says "changes nothing else", which I read as text and comments too. If the owner reads it as parsed content only, drop that one case. It is its own node.
- **Reading beyond I2.** I2 (i) includes the WBS-id form (`names-by-wbs`): a roster naming `P-01` counts as naming an existing ticket, as the guard resolves it. An implementer who checks only `<id>.md` would create a second ticket and fail those two cases. It is a defensible reading, but it goes past what I2 states.
- **Narrow predicate.** The "claims a key was set" predicate flags only the phrases listed in README § "Success 2: the words". A false claim worded another way would pass.
- **Real refusal wording.** Success-2's "does not claim" cases are red on the base only because of "(set at adoption)". A real fix may avoid every listed phrase and still mislead, which a narrow predicate cannot see. The README says so.
lessons:
- The brief's scratch locations (`/tmp/gov-os-lead-<ticket>`, `.gov-runtime/scratch/td/`) are not writable in this sandbox. The launcher should point the designer at the sandbox's `$TMPDIR`. This cost a few minutes.
- A bite-check flaw can be satisfied by an unrelated path: `set_up` already listed both files in A0's record, so my first `record_silent` stand-in passed. Always confirm the first red of a new stand-in.
proposed_decisions: none. No KPI line needed a guessed interface. The three readings above are stated in the README, not asked.

- Whether "`<project>`" is the folder name, as in reading 1. The engineer's A0 will show which name it derives.
recommended_next_action: The CTO routes the engineer. Tell the engineer to keep "Set the top-level key" in the refusal, or widen the ticket by the unit test file. Run the suite from the ticket worktree (`gov accept W2-113`) after the merge. Before the owner reads this, decide whether readings 6 (WBS-id form) and 7 (the comments case) stand.
